answer: Juniper-tagged answer minting. Each identity gets a one-time task whose correct output must embed a random token drawn from a public entropy beacon, so every answer is valid exactly once and republishing it fails verification. An attacker cloning identities must solve each fresh task independently, paying full compute per clone. A jade watermark in the payload exposes copied replies, and a copper hash of the beacon round is checked at submission, so stale or recycled answers are rejected outright.
